reason: Technic Panel Fairing Smooth #5 leaks along a slit 0.075 LDU wide and 52 long.
The top face of the lower body (y = -8) ends at x = 6 for z = 34..86: the quads of lines 18 and 20,
the 4-4ndis/3-4ndis of lines 44 and 46 (radius 6) and the 1-4ring2 of s\64683s01.dat line 312.
The strip that face turns up into, line 14 (y = -8.558..-7), stands at x = 6.075, under the edge the
shell's inner surface starts from (lines 76, 82, 91 all use 6.075), and the quad of line 19 meets it
there for z = 86..89. So between z = 34 and 86 nothing spans x = 6..6.075.
The patch adds one quad on the plane y = -8 from x = 5 to 6.5, z = 34..86: it lies on the existing
top face, closes the slit and ends inside the body behind the strip. It adds no volume of its own;
a face exactly 0.075 wide would be narrower than the tolerance the mesh is mended with.
The Power Functions battery box's mounting brackets leak at eight strips 0.08-0.12 LDU wide.
The bracket's outer wall is a radius-9 cylinder drawn with 1-16cyli.dat (lines 120 and 178), which
ends at the 16-gon's vertex x = 3.44415, y = -/+48.31492. The flat face that continues it, lines 43
and 152 (edge lines 45 and 154), starts at x = 3.56, y = -/+48.314: the same corner placed on the true
circle (radius 9.044, 23.2 degrees) instead of on the 16-gon (22.5 degrees). That leaves a strip
0.116 LDU wide down the side and a sliver outside the 2-4ring8 end faces (lines 131 and 189).
The patch moves the two faces' outer corners onto the vertex the cylinder ends at; the subpart is
placed four times (s\919s02.dat lines 11-12, each with both brackets), which is the eight strips.
Power Functions XL motor, front shell. The file says "Needs Work: Inner side not modelled" (line 11), and the inside
is indeed not drawn, but nothing has to be authored for it: the outer surface of the motor (this shell, 59154.dat and
47157.dat) encloses the inside on its own once the places where its faces miss each other are mended, and the region
builder fills it - the solid is the filled housing, its volume the envelope's, not the plastic's. The surfaces the
missing inner side would have joined (the 1-4disc pocket floors at z = 10, the bosses behind the front holes) stay
where they are, inside the solid. Two of the misses are in this file:
1. The front ring and inner cone around the peg holes at (0, -/+40) share the corner (-/+8.45, -/+37.05, 0)
(lines 290-303, 399-412), a point of the true circle of radius 9 that stands 0.03 LDU outside the 16-gon of the
boss it meets (2-4cyli, lines 81, 83, 103, 105), leaving a hole at each corner. The corner is moved onto that
16-gon's edge, (-/+8.415, -/+37.057, 0), in every face and edge line that uses it.
2. The side holes' sloped channels (1-4cyls2, lines 131-133 and 171-173) end at (-/+24, -/+8, 10), but the boss
they run into (2-4cyli of radius 9 about (-/+20, 0), lines 24 and 52) is at x = -/+23.916 there, as the edge lines
143, 151, 183 and 191 draw it: a sliver 0.08 wide is open. A quad continues each channel's last facet 0.5 LDU along
its own plane, into the boss.
Power Functions XL motor, back shell; "Needs Work: Inner side not modelled" (line 11), as for 59155.dat, whose
entry says why nothing has to be authored for that. Two places where this shell's faces miss:
1. It meets 59155.dat at z = -89 (z = 21 in 58121), where 59155's wall ends in a ring on the 48-gon of radius 48
(48\1-8rin39, its lines 202, 214, 226, 238). This shell's side ridges peak on the true circle instead: their
are at r = 48.0, up to 0.1 LDU outside the 48-gon, so each ridge's foot overhangs the ring with nothing under it.
Quads at z = -89 run from each ridge's bottom edges (the peak and the faces either side, r = 47-48) in to
r = 46.9: on the ring where the ring is, closing the overhang where it is not.
2. The side windows' quads 41 and 132 end at z = -8.2, where their corner (-/+49.36, -/+3.7) is just outside the
16-gon of the boss (4-4cyli of radius 9, lines 23 and 32); the quads beside them (38, 47, 129, 138) end at
z = -8, inside it. They are made to end at z = -8 too.
Power Functions IR remote, bottom half. Quad 99, the inner wall that slopes down to the boss of the hole in 58134.dat
(lines 84-102, a 4-4cyli of radius 9 about x = 0, z = 74), has its top corner at (4, 0, 82) in the part: a point of the
true circle of radius 9, but the boss is a 16-gon, at z = 81.94 for x = 4, so the corner stands 0.05 LDU outside it
and leaves the wall, the boss and the strip on top (58134.dat line 25) a gap to the outside. The corner is moved to
x = 3.5, inside the boss's wall, where the wall ends. The subpart is placed twice, mirrored, so both sides are mended.
The file also says "Needs Work: Internal surface not exact"; nothing is authored for that.
58134 builds 10,656 mm^3 against 10,148 +- 58 sampled. Every sample on which the two disagree is inside the solid
and has a winding number of 0.32-0.5 - all of them in the side walls that carry the Technic beam (32524) at
x = -/+41..49: the surface's winding there sits up to 0.3 below its whole value, where the beam overlaps the walls,
while crossing the outer wall still raises it by 0.7-1.0. The sampled estimate's 0.5 threshold drops those walls;
the solid keeps them.
Power Functions IR remote, top half. LDraw leaves out its inside: the header says "Needs Work: Inside not modelled"
(line 11), and the file draws the outer skin only, so the half is open underneath along a 67-vertex rim that runs
from y = -47 along the sides up to y = -24 at the ends, round the window for the front glass, and round the channel
selector's slot, whose floor is not drawn either.
Authored, to the filled-envelope convention - the skin closed across its own open rim and nothing else:
- the underside: a ruled surface across the rim, a flat strip between each pair of matching rim vertices left and
right (the rim is symmetric in x), so it is flat at y = -47 along the sides and rises with the rim to y = -38,
-32 and -24 at the ends; every vertex is a vertex of the drawn rim;
- the glass window: closed by the plane through its two straight top edges (x = -/+19, from (y, z) = (-56, -99) to
(-58.32, -53.25)) and by the plane z = -99 between its two straight front edges;
- the selector slot: its floor, a quad between the bottom edges of its drawn walls (s\58132s01.dat line 354) and a
1-4chrd on the bottom edge of each rounded end (the matrices of that subpart's 1-4edge lines 350 and 353).
Deviation from the real part: the top half is a thin shell; here it is solid down to its rim (58132 alone:
17,532 mm^3, against 17,442 +- 53 sampled), and its slot is a pocket with a flat floor where the real one opens into
the remote. Nothing reaches beyond the rim, so the bounding box is the LDraw geometry's. In 58122 the underside
lies on 58134's top along the sides and above 58134 elsewhere; the space between it, 58134's plate and inner walls
and the battery lid is a closed cavity, which the solid keeps (those walls are drawn facing into it).
Power Functions IR remote, top half, the subpart 58132.dat places twice (the second mirrored in x). Two places where
the same surface is drawn twice a hair apart, which leave no closed body once the half's inside is closed:
1. Quad 417, the top in front of the selector's slot, has a straight edge from (0, 27.81) to (8, 31) in the part,
running across the 1-4ring6 of 58132.dat line 24, whose plane is 0.002-0.003 LDU off its own. It becomes three
triangles that stop on the ring's outer edge - its vertices (0, 27.8) and (5.05, 28.808), and its next edge's point
2. The slot's rounded ends, the 1-4cyli of lines 349 and 352, each span the whole slot (x = -8 to 8), so the two
placements draw them twice, triangulated differently; in 58122 the channel selector's matching rounded end lies on
them too. Each becomes a 1-8cyli with the same matrix: one half of the end per placement.
Technic Panel Smooth 11 x 2 x 3, one half (62531.dat places it twice, mirrored in z). Its slot ends, stepped
cylinders against a curve drawn only by edge lines, turned out not to leak: closed between two planes every 2 LDU,
every section through them closes. The leaks were at the end of the beam, z = -/+69..73 and -/+87..89, by the
horizontal pin hole at z = -/+80, where surfaces are drawn twice a hair apart:
1. Line 203 (a 2-4cyli of radius 9, x = -20..-12) draws half the pin hole's boss again over the 7-8cyli of line 206
(x = -30..-12), to fill the eighth the 7-8cyli leaves out. It becomes a 1-8cyli covering only that eighth.
2. Line 211, the curved roof over the hole, is a 1-4cyli of scale 8.001, so its edges end at y = -27.999 and
z = -88.001 / -71.999, 0.001 off the faces at z = -88 and -72 they meet (lines 51 and 70, which end at y = -28).
The scale is made 8, there and in its edge line 210.
3. Quad 448 lies within 0.0003 of the plane of quad 411 and overlaps it. Its corners are put on that plane and its
top edge on 411's bottom edge, so the two meet instead.
62531 then builds 6,041.9 mm^3 against 6,018 +- 28 sampled, with the LDraw geometry's bounding box. Nothing is
